summary: Phase 4 test specs for mo-execute-and-fulfill. 24 Playwright e2e specs (no Vitest, no mocks, no @testing-library) — 6 fast write-path smoke specs + 18 slow operational stories. Each spec maps 1:1 to a scenario S01-S24 (S23/S24 added per critic), uses the repo's `test`/`db`/`testFetch` fixtures, hits the real API with the seeded org's session cookie, and asserts DB state via the RLS-scoped `db` fixture. Idempotency-Key semantics are critical: `testFetch` derives a deterministic key from method+path+body fingerprint, so same body = same key by default. For SAME-KEY replay tests we override headers explicitly; for race scenarios we use Promise.allSettled and identify winners by response shape, not array order. Critic findings applied inline: S06 demoted to P1, S11 tightened to status===500 with TODO flag-flip note, S15 split (batch-mode parent rejection retained, discrete+batchId case dropped), S23 + S24 added as fast first-attempt 409 representatives.

Companion invariant spec shipping with this PR series — referenced for snapshot-and-diff style.

inferences: testFetch derives Idempotency-Key as `test:METHOD:path:bodyFingerprint` (helpers/api.ts 138-151). For same-key replay you MUST override headers explicitly with `Idempotency-Key: 'K1'`. For different-key on same body, override is also required since the default is body-derived.
Race scenarios (S21, S22) settle in non-deterministic order. Identify winner/loser by response.status and response.body, never by array index.
BR-10 absence assertions use `COUNT(*)` snapshots filtered by orgId+shipmentId+timestamp boundary. The test must snapshot BEFORE the cost edit and re-snapshot AFTER, asserting equality.

BR-12 reversal scenarios MUST assert: produced lot.quantity decremented, ingredient lots restocked, inventory_events with eventType='manufacturing_variance_gain' present — three independent invariants with a self-documenting failure message.
Products in tests must be created with `sellable: true` to appear on sales order lines (createItem helper passes through; default in schema is false).
Dates (orderDate, shipDate) must be computed at call time from `new Date()` so they don't go stale as the calendar rolls.
unknowns: Exact UI selectors for /execute Mark done / Complete order / Start batch buttons. These specs are API-first (no UI navigation required for the assertions); slow specs that visit /execute should look up selectors against manufacturing-execution.tsx during test authoring.

Whether the /api/manufacturing-orders/[id]/execution GET endpoint always lists ingredients in BOM order; the existing pickAllManufacturingIngredients helper iterates whatever order is returned, which is sufficient for the assertion semantics here.

Exact API path for the materializeManufacturingOutputAllocationFromExistingOutputInTx side-effect on second /complete after a prior /outputs call — not exercised in this batch beyond S04 which uses outputDisposition='blocked' to bypass it.

fixtures: import { test, expect } from '../fixtures';  // custom test with auto-injected session cookie + RLS-scoped `db` fixture
Use `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` for any spec where tests share data via describe-level `let` variables.
Use the `db` fixture for all DB assertions — it uses app_user with RLS, same security path as the app.
api_helpers: testFetch(path, options) — auto-includes Origin, Cookie, Content-Type; derives Idempotency-Key from `test:METHOD:path:bodyFingerprint`. Override via `headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'K1' }` for same-key replay or distinct-key races.
createItem({ ..., sellable: true }) — sellable defaults to false; products on sales order lines must opt in.
createCustomer({ name }) — minimum payload; returns { status, body: { id } }.
createSalesOrder({ customerId, lines, shipments?, ... }) — orderDate/shipDate must be computed via new Date() at call time.
confirmSalesOrder(orderId, { confirmOversell }) — required to move SO from draft into 'open' state with reservations.
createManufacturingOrder({ productId, plannedQuantity, ingredients, confirmShortage: true }) — confirmShortage=true to bypass insufficient-stock guard at create time.
releaseManufacturingOrder(orderId, { confirmShortage: true }) — required to enter the execute-and-fulfill surface.

completeManufacturingOrder(orderId, actualQuantity, { outputDisposition? }) — wraps POST /complete; specs needing extra body fields (ingredientActuals, confirmNegativeStock) must call testFetch directly.
db_assertion_patterns: Numeric columns return strings — use parseFloat() or formatQuantity() for comparisons; never compare strings of trimmed-vs-untrimmed scale.
Filter master rows with isNull(items.deletedAt) when asserting against soft-deleted entities.
Aggregate snapshots: const beforeCount = (await db.select({ c: sql<string>`COUNT(*)` }).from(inventoryEvents).where(...))[0].c — then after, assert equality.

Subtype + reference filter: select where eq(inventoryEvents.eventType, 'manufacturing_variance_gain') AND eq(inventoryEvents.referenceType, 'manufacturing_order') AND eq(inventoryEvents.referenceId, orderId).
Stock allocation snapshots: select where eq(stockAllocations.demandType, 'sales_shipment_line') AND eq(stockAllocations.demandId, shipmentLineId).
idempotency_helpers: Default behaviour: same body -> same derived key -> server replay returns cached envelope.
Explicit same-key replay (S19/S20): pass `headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'K1' }` on BOTH calls.
Distinct-key replay (S05/S07 first-vs-second attempt with different body): testFetch will derive different keys automatically because the body fingerprint changes between attempts.
Mismatched-key 409 (S19 third call): pass `headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'K1' }` with a CHANGED body — server detects paramsHash mismatch -> IdempotencyConflictError 409.
race_patterns: Fire concurrent requests via Promise.allSettled. After settle, identify winner by response.status===2xx and loser by response.status===4xx or by checking body.error. Do NOT identify by array order.
Lock-serialised races (S21): exactly-one-2xx assertion via a count of fulfilled-with-status-200 promises.
Cost-basis commutativity (S22): compute expected items.currentStockUnitCost INDEPENDENT of completion order via the running weighted-average formula.
common_setup: Use `Date.now()` + `Math.random().toString(36)` suffixes on every created entity name to avoid collisions between parallel workers.
Compute dates via `new Date()` and offset with `+ N * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000` for future ship dates.
All material defaults: `defaultPurchasePrice: '<non-null>'` so cost basis can resolve on positive flows.
All product defaults: `sellable: true` and BOM with at least one non-deleted ingredient line — otherwise the new-MO product picker rejects.
naming_conventions: Test names: short verb phrase, no leading 'should'. Match the scenario title.
Variables shared across serial tests: declared at the `test.describe` block as `let varName: string` and assigned in the first test.
Fixture suffix: `_${ts}` or `_${Date.now()}` on every name/sku to keep parallel-worker isolation.

test_specs.test_name: drives discrete MO release -> pick -> complete -> downstream SO ship end-to-end
test_specs.purpose: End-to-end regression smoke for the entire feature: cost basis non-null on produced lot, MO promise materialises onto produced lot, shipment consumes lot hold first, expected_qty zeros at complete, parent SO flips to done after ship.

preconditions: Material item with stock and defaultPurchasePrice set so cost basis resolves
Product item with sellable=true and BOM referencing the material
Customer fixture
Confirmed sales order linked to the product
Manufacturing order created and released (confirmShortage: true) linked to the SO line
seed_data: Sales order: 1 line of product qty='10' unitPrice='50.00', confirmed
Manufacturing order: plannedQuantity='10', ingredients=[{itemId: materialId, quantityPerUnit: '2'}], released

interaction_plan: Fetch /api/manufacturing-orders/[id]/execution to enumerate ingredient ids
For each ingredient: POST /api/manufacturing-orders/[id]/ingredients/[ingredientId]/pick with body '{}' (testFetch derives Idempotency-Key automatically)
POST /api/manufacturing-orders/[id]/complete body { actualQuantity: '10', outputDisposition: 'available' }
Plan shipment: POST /api/sales-orders/[id]/shipments body { fulfillmentType: 'delivery', scheduledDate: <date+7d>, deliveryDate: <date+7d>, lines: [{ salesOrderLineId, quantity: '10' }] }
POST /api/sales-orders/[id]/shipments/[shipmentId]/ship body { syncAccounting: false }

behavioral: Every pick response status === 200; body has ingredient id matching url
side_effects: manufacturingOrderIngredients.pickStatus === 'picked' for every ingredient row of the MO
manufacturingOrders.status === 'done' and completedAt non-null after /complete
manufacturingOrders.actualCostPerUnit non-null and > 0
Exactly one lots row exists with itemId === productId and unitCost > 0
stockAllocations where demandType==='manufacturing_order_ingredient' AND demandId IN ingredients of this MO -> all rows have status==='consumed'

stockAllocations where demandType==='sales_shipment_line' AND demandId === shipmentLineId -> at least one row has sourceType==='inventory_lot' pointing to the produced lot after /complete (materialisation step)
After ship: stockAllocations for this shipment-line all rows status==='consumed'
salesShipments.status === 'shipped' and shippedAt non-null
salesOrders.status === 'done' (single-line order, fully shipped)
inventoryEvents has rows with eventType==='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' (one per ingredient) AND eventType==='manufacturing_output' AND eventType==='sales_consumption' for the shipped lot
inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty for productId returns to 0 after /complete (residual released)
negative_assertions: No row of stockAllocations(demandType='sales_shipment_line', demandId=shipmentLineId, sourceType='manufacturing_order', status='active') remains after the MO completes (materialisation should replace it)
Ship does NOT 409 — the materialised lot hold satisfies the shipment line

waiting_strategy: Each testFetch awaits before the next call — no implicit polling required.
After /complete + before /ship, no UI poll is needed since API calls are synchronous; assertions read DB directly via `db` fixture.
flakiness_risks: Date drift if shipDate is hardcoded; compute via `new Date()` + offset.
Allocation row counts can drift if a parallel worker mutates the same product — keep names/SKUs unique with ts+random suffix.
Order of inventoryEvents rows depends on transaction insert order; assert by COUNT and by filtered presence, not by array index.
data_isolation_notes: All entities suffixed with `ts = Date.now()`; product/material/customer all carry the same suffix for traceability.
Each test in this spec file is at describe-level scope so variables shared via `let` survive but DB rows are unique.
applicable_helpers: testFetch for /shipments and /ship endpoints (no dedicated helper yet)
new_helpers_recommended: Consider adding helpers/api.ts shipments helper for parity: createShipment(orderId, payload), shipShipment(orderId, shipmentId, payload). Optional — testFetch direct is fine.

test_specs.test_name: batch-mode MO produces one lot per batch and parent flips only on final batch
test_specs.purpose: Assert BR-6 (exactly one lot per batch) and BR-7 (parent stays 'open' until final batch). Manufacturing-actuals fast spec already exercises this for the happy path; this slow story extends to assert distinct lotIds per batch and inventoryEvents structure.

preconditions: Material with sufficient stock for 2 batches
Product with manufacturingMode='batch', expectedBatchYield='50', BOM with per_batch consumption
Released batch-mode MO with exactly 2 manufacturing_order_batches rows in 'pending'
seed_data: Product: bom=[{componentId: materialId, quantity: '1', recipeBasis: 'batch', outputQuantity: '50'}]

interaction_plan: Read manufacturingOrderBatches for the MO, sort by batchNumber
For batch1: POST /batches/[b1]/start, then pick b1 ingredient(s), then POST /batches/[b1]/complete with actualQuantity='50'
Snapshot parent MO: SELECT status, completedAt FROM manufacturingOrders WHERE id = orderId
For batch2: POST /batches/[b2]/start, pick, complete
Snapshot final state

behavioral: After batch1 complete: parent MO.status === 'open' and completedAt === null
After batch2 complete: parent MO.status === 'done' and completedAt non-null
side_effects: manufacturingOrderBatches[batch1].lotId non-null after batch1 complete
manufacturingOrderBatches[batch2].lotId non-null after batch2 complete
batch1.lotId !== batch2.lotId (distinct lots, BR-6)
Two distinct lots rows exist with itemId === productId, each unitCost > 0
manufacturingOrderOutputs has exactly 2 rows for the MO, one per batch
manufacturingOrders.actualQuantity === '100.0000' after batch2
inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty for productId is 0 after batch2 completes (residual released via T_PARENT_DONE)
negative_assertions: No /complete on the parent MO is required or expected — only batch /complete endpoints are used
No row in lots has unitCost === null or 0

flakiness_risks: Per-batch ingredient lookup must filter by manufacturingOrderBatchId — see fast/manufacturing-actuals.spec.ts pattern.

test_specs.test_name: ship 409 when shipment line has unmaterialised manufacturing_order source; override does not bypass; succeeds after MO completes
test_specs.purpose: BR-14 wait-for-MO guard: consumeForShipmentInTx refuses fall-through even with confirmNegativeStock=true. Verified against lib/inventory/kernel/operations/sales.ts:756-768 — the throw at 763 is NOT gated by params.allowNegativeStock.

preconditions: Customer + product (sellable=true) with BOM
Confirmed SO for the product with quantity that requires the MO to produce
Sales-linked MO created from the SO line, released (so stock_allocations sourceType='manufacturing_order' is active on the shipment line)
No other free stock for the product so plain FIFO would also fail
Planned shipment covering the SO line
MO ingredients UNPICKED so no production has occurred
seed_data: Material stock high enough for MO consumption
Product: stock='0', no existing lots for the product
Sales order quantity equals MO plannedQuantity

interaction_plan: Verify precondition: stockAllocations(demandType='sales_shipment_line', demandId=shipmentLineId, sourceType='manufacturing_order', status='active') row exists
Call 1: POST /shipments/[shipmentId]/ship body { syncAccounting: false } — expect 409 negativeStock
Call 2: POST same path body { syncAccounting: false, confirmNegativeStock: true } — expect 409 still (override does not bypass wait-for-MO; testFetch derives a different key because body differs)
Pick all MO ingredients then POST /complete with outputDisposition='available'
Call 3: POST /shipments/[shipmentId]/ship body { syncAccounting: false } — expect 200

behavioral: Call 1: status === 409; body.error matches /Insufficient stock|Not enough/; body.negativeStock present with { itemId, itemName, available, requested, shortage }
Call 2: status === 409; same negativeStock payload shape (wait-for-MO uses identical SalesError translation)
side_effects: Between Calls 1 and 2: no new inventoryEvents rows for this shipment (assert COUNT unchanged)
Between Calls 1 and 2: salesShipments.status remains 'planned'
After /complete: stockAllocations row for the shipment-line flips from sourceType='manufacturing_order' to sourceType='inventory_lot' (materialisation)

applicable_helpers: createItem, createCustomer, createSalesOrder, confirmSalesOrder, createManufacturingOrder, releaseManufacturingOrder, testFetch

test_specs.test_name: outputDisposition='blocked' bypasses materialisation; downstream ship 409s with same payload
test_specs.purpose: BR-13: produceManufacturedStockInTx skips materializeManufacturingOrderSourceAllocationsForLotInTx when outputDisposition='blocked'. Downstream shipment with an unmaterialised MO source still 409s.

preconditions: Same setup as S03 — sales-linked MO with planned shipment carrying MO-source allocation
MO ingredients picked

POST /outputs body { quantity: '10', outputDisposition: 'blocked' }
POST /complete body { actualQuantity: '10', outputDisposition: 'blocked' }
POST /shipments/[shipmentId]/ship body { syncAccounting: false } — expect 409

behavioral: Output recorded and complete both return 200
side_effects: Produced lots row exists; inventoryLotBalances row for the lot has disposition='blocked'
stockAllocations(demandType='sales_shipment_line', demandId=shipmentLineId, sourceType='manufacturing_order', status='active') still present (NOT materialised)
No stockAllocations row of sourceType='inventory_lot' against the produced lot for this shipment line

test_specs.test_name: pick 409 stock_shortage and confirmNegativeStock override creates NEG synthetic lot
test_specs.purpose: BR-3a + BR-4a: pickManufacturingIngredient surfaces shortage.warningType='stock_shortage' and override creates a NEG-<date>-<uuid> lot with resolved cost basis.

preconditions: Released discrete MO with one material ingredient whose plannedQuantity > current available stock
Material has non-null currentStockUnitCost or defaultPurchasePrice
seed_data: MO plannedQuantity='10' with ingredient quantityPerUnit='1' (requires 10 of material, only 5 on hand)

interaction_plan: POST /pick body {} (no confirm flag) — expect 409 stock_shortage
POST /pick body { confirmNegativeStock: true } — testFetch derives a different key due to body fingerprint change; expect 200

behavioral: Call 1: status === 409; body.shortage present with warningType==='stock_shortage' and itemName populated (matches ManufacturingError extra payload)
side_effects: After Call 1: COUNT(manufacturingPickAllocations where manufacturingOrderIngredientId === ingredient.id) === 0
After Call 2: at least one lots row exists with lotNumber LIKE 'NEG-%' and itemId === material.id and unitCost > 0
After Call 2: inventoryEvents has rows for the ingredient with eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' referencing the NEG lot OR the existing lot
manufacturingOrderIngredients.pickStatus === 'picked' after Call 2
negative_assertions: Call 1 writes zero new inventoryEvents for the ingredient
No row in lots has unitCost === null

flakiness_risks: NEG-lot detection by lotNumber LIKE 'NEG-%' is implementation-detail; an alternative is to assert that COUNT(lots WHERE itemId=materialId) increased by 1 across Call 2.

test_specs.test_name: pick 409 requirement_violation (minimum lot age) and confirmRequirementOverride
test_specs.purpose: BR-3b: requirement_violation 409 with nextEligibleDate. Demoted to P1 per critic — shares DAL surface with S05 so marginal regression value is lower.

Material stock exists but every lot's receivedAt is INSIDE the minimum age window
Released MO whose ingredient references this material
seed_data: Lots created via createItem opening balance have receivedAt = now (inside window)

interaction_plan: POST /pick body {} — expect 409 requirement_violation
POST /pick body { confirmRequirementOverride: true } — expect 200

side_effects: After Call 2: manufacturingPickAllocations row for this ingredient has requirementOverrideConfirmed === true
After Call 2: requirementOverrideConfirmedBy and requirementOverrideConfirmedAt non-null
inventoryEvents includes eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' for the ingredient
negative_assertions: Call 1 inserts zero pick_allocations rows

test_specs.test_name: ship 409 negativeStock (plain shortage, no MO promise) and confirmNegativeStock override creates NEG lot
test_specs.purpose: BR-3c + BR-4b: shipSalesShipment translates InsufficientStockError to SalesError 409 negativeStock; override path creates synthetic NEG lot via createNegativeStockEventInTx with cost resolved via product BOM cost-walk.

preconditions: Product with active BOM (so resolvePositiveStockUnitCostInTx product branch can succeed)
Stock=0 for the product (or below the shipment quantity)
Confirmed SO for the product with quantity > available
Planned shipment with NO MO-source allocation on the line
seed_data: Material: stock='100', defaultPurchasePrice='5.00' (cost basis for product BOM walk)
Product: sellable=true, stock='0', bom=[{componentId: materialId, quantity: '1'}]

interaction_plan: POST /shipments/[shipmentId]/ship body { syncAccounting: false } — expect 409
POST same path body { syncAccounting: false, confirmNegativeStock: true } — expect 200

behavioral: Call 1: status === 409; body.negativeStock present with shape { itemId, itemName, available, requested, shortage }
side_effects: After Call 1: salesShipments.status === 'planned' (unchanged); COUNT(inventoryEvents where referenceType='sales_shipment' AND referenceId=shipmentId) === 0
After Call 2: a lots row exists with lotNumber LIKE 'NEG-%' and itemId === productId and unitCost > 0
After Call 2: inventoryEvents includes eventType='sales_consumption' for the shipment
After Call 2: salesShipments.status === 'shipped' and shippedAt non-null
negative_assertions: Call 1 does NOT create any NEG lot

test_specs.purpose: BR-11 missing-pick guard. Cheap fast-lane assertion: 400 with ingredient name in error; MO status unchanged.

Only ONE ingredient picked
seed_data: Two materials with stock + cost basis

interaction_plan: POST /complete body { actualQuantity: '10' }

behavioral: body.error matches /Pick/i and contains the unpicked ingredient's item name
side_effects: manufacturingOrders.status === 'open' (unchanged)
manufacturingOrders.completedAt === null
No new inventoryEvents of eventType='manufacturing_output' for this MO
negative_assertions: No new lots row created for the product
No row in manufacturingOrderOutputs for the MO

test_specs.test_name: material weighted-average cost on positive flow into existing lot
test_specs.purpose: BR-4a: appendPositiveStockToExistingLotInTx weighted-averages lot quantity AND unitCost; calculateNextCurrentStockUnitCost mirrors it into items.currentStockUnitCost.

preconditions: Material with one existing lot (qty=100, unitCost=10.000000)
items.currentStockUnitCost = 10.000000
seed_data: createItem stock='100', defaultPurchasePrice='10.00' — creates one lot via opening balance

interaction_plan: Capture lot row id from createItem

Trigger a positive append: simplest is a manual adjustment increase via POST /api/items/[id]/adjust (or via a purchase receipt) with quantity=50, unitCost=14.00 targeting the SAME lot (lotNumber from the existing lot)
Re-read items.currentStockUnitCost and lots.unitCost

side_effects: lots row after: quantity === '150.0000', unitCost === '11.333333' (or matches (100*10+50*14)/150 at scale 6)
items.currentStockUnitCost === '11.333333' after the append
negative_assertions: No second lots row was created — the append updated the existing lot in place

Test author must confirm the exact API surface (POST /api/items/[id]/adjust or similar) supports lotNumber targeting; otherwise mock the append by issuing two purchase receipts to the same supplier+lotNumber.
Floating-point comparison: use string-equality after trimScale, or parseFloat + toBeCloseTo(11.333333, 6).
new_helpers_recommended: Adjust-stock helper if not already present in test/helpers/api.ts (manualIncreaseStock pattern).

test_specs.test_name: expected supply deltas across release / output / complete / cancel
test_specs.purpose: BR-5: items.expectedQty is event-driven via subtypes manufacturing_release / manufacturing_complete / cancel. End-to-end walk of two MOs through release/partial-output/complete/cancel.

preconditions: Product item with zero current expectedQty
Two discrete MOs ready (MO-A and MO-B) referencing the product

interaction_plan: Release MO-A (call release API or via createManufacturingOrder + releaseManufacturingOrder)
Snapshot inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty for productId
Release MO-B; snapshot
Pick MO-A ingredients; POST /outputs quantity='4'; snapshot
POST /complete on MO-A actualQuantity='10'; snapshot
DELETE /api/manufacturing-orders/[MO-B] (cancel); snapshot

side_effects: After release MO-A: inventoryItemBalances.expectedQty for productId === '10.0000' (or parseFloat === 10)
After release MO-B: expectedQty === '25.0000' (10 + 15)
After /outputs quantity 4 on MO-A: expectedQty === '21.0000' (25 - 4)
After /complete MO-A (full release of residual): expectedQty === '15.0000' (just MO-B left)
After /delete MO-B: expectedQty === '0.0000'

inventoryEvents has rows with eventType='expected_increase' or eventSubtype='manufacturing_release' (2 — one per MO), eventType='expected_release' or eventSubtype='manufacturing_complete' (for the output + completion + cancel paths)
negative_assertions: No drift: final expectedQty === 0 EXACTLY after MO-B cancel

flakiness_risks: expectedQty drift between snapshots can be off-by-rounding; use parseFloat + toBeCloseTo(value, 4) for comparisons.
If MO-A has actualQuantity overrun (e.g. /outputs creates 4 then /complete with actualQuantity=10 produces 6 more), the test must compute expected deltas from inputs not assume static values.

Produced lot NOT yet consumed by any shipment (assert COUNT(stockAllocations where sourceType='inventory_lot' AND sourceId=producedLotId AND status='consumed') === 0)

test_specs.test_name: pick on already-fully-picked ingredient returns 400 'is already picked'
test_specs.purpose: Cheap fast-lane guard: pick endpoint rejects re-pick of fully-picked ingredient; no new allocations.

preconditions: Released discrete MO with one ingredient picked
seed_data: Standard material+product, MO planned=10, pick the single ingredient

interaction_plan: Snapshot COUNT(manufacturingPickAllocations where ingredient.id) === N

POST /pick on the same ingredient — testFetch derives a unique key from method+path+body so this is treated as a NEW request, NOT a replay (body='{}' identical to first call would normally collide via key, so we must force a DIFFERENT key by passing headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'fresh-' + Date.now() }) OR by passing a non-empty body like { reason: 'retry' } if the schema accepts unknown fields. SIMPLER: pass headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': `retry-${ts}` } to force a distinct key.

side_effects: COUNT(manufacturingPickAllocations where ingredient.id) === N (unchanged)
No new inventoryEvents for this MO since the original pick
negative_assertions: No second 'manufacturing_pick' or 'picked' subtype event

flakiness_risks: Without forcing a distinct Idempotency-Key, the second call would return the cached envelope (200) instead of triggering the already-picked guard. The test MUST pass `headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': 'retry-' + Date.now() }`.

test_specs.test_name: idempotent ship replay: same key returns cached body; ledger unchanged; mismatched body returns 409 conflict
test_specs.purpose: BR-9: shipSalesShipment idempotency replay. Must use SAME explicit Idempotency-Key on both calls (override testFetch default) since default would derive a NEW key from the same body — though same body would coincide, the explicit override makes the intent explicit and survives helper changes. Third call with same key + changed body must 409.

preconditions: Confirmed SO with planned shipment and sufficient free stock for the line

interaction_plan: Idempotency-Key K1 = `mo-execute-and-fulfill:ship:${ts}`
Body B = { syncAccounting: false }

Call 2: POST /ship with headers { 'Idempotency-Key': K1 } body B — capture R2
Call 3: POST /ship with headers { 'Idempotency-Key': K1 } body B' = { syncAccounting: true } — capture R3

side_effects: Between R1 and R2: COUNT(inventoryEvents where referenceType='sales_shipment' AND referenceId=shipmentId) UNCHANGED
Between R1 and R2: COUNT(inventoryLotBalances mutations for the consumed item) UNCHANGED
Between R1 and R2: salesShipments.shippedAt UNCHANGED (still the R1 timestamp)
Between R2 and R3: salesShipments.shippedAt UNCHANGED
negative_assertions: R2 does NOT create a second sales_consumption event
R3 does NOT mutate any inventory state

flakiness_risks: MUST pass explicit headers on each call. testFetch default would derive different keys for B vs B' so the conflict test wouldn't fire without override.
shipSalesShipment Xero block runs outside tx; assert against integrations.audit_events filtered by created_at > pre-snapshot.

test_specs.test_name: idempotent pick + complete replay: same key returns cached body; no double-deduct

Call P2: POST /pick on ingredient I with headers { 'Idempotency-Key': K1 } body '{}' — capture R-P2
Pick any remaining ingredients (without explicit key — testFetch default is fine)

Call C2: POST /complete with headers { 'Idempotency-Key': K2 } body { actualQuantity: '10' } — capture R-C2

R-C1 and R-C2 status === 200; bodies deeply equal

COUNT(manufacturingOrderOutputs for MO) after C2 === count after C1 (exactly 1)
COUNT(lots where itemId = productId) after C2 === count after C1 (exactly 1)
manufacturingOrders.actualQuantity unchanged between C1 and C2

No second status flip (status='done' stable)

test_specs.test_name: concurrent pick on same ingredient: row lock serialises; exactly one 200, the other 400 already-picked
test_specs.purpose: BR-15 row lock invariant. Identify winner/loser by response shape, not array order.

preconditions: Released discrete MO with one ingredient unpicked
Sufficient stock so either call could individually succeed without override

interaction_plan: Build two distinct Idempotency-Keys K-A and K-B (so the calls are not replays of each other)
Fire two POST /pick requests in parallel via Promise.allSettled([fetchA, fetchB])
Map results to { status, body } pairs
Identify winner = the result with status===200; loser = the other

behavioral: The OTHER response has status === 400 AND body.error matches /already picked/i
Winner is identified by response.status, NOT by array index
side_effects: COUNT(manufacturingPickAllocations where ingredient = I) equals the winner's allocation count (typically 1 row covering the full planned quantity, NOT double)
manufacturingOrderIngredients.pickStatus === 'picked' (exactly once)
negative_assertions: No partial-pick state visible
No second 'manufacturing_pick' event

flakiness_risks: Both Idempotency-Keys must be DISTINCT — otherwise the second call is a replay and returns 200 cached, not 400 already-picked.
Under exotic conditions both calls could be serialised and the second call's locked row read shows 'already picked' BEFORE the FOR UPDATE — same outcome.
On rare Postgres deadlock retries this could surface a 500 from a third path; if observed, add a deadlock retry note and re-run.

test_specs.test_name: concurrent /complete on two MOs producing into same product: cost basis weighted-average commutative under serialised commits
test_specs.purpose: Cost-basis race: items.currentStockUnitCost must equal cumulative weighted average regardless of commit order (calculateNextCurrentStockUnitCost is commutative for (qty,unitCost) pairs).

preconditions: Two released discrete MOs (MO-A, MO-B) both producing into the SAME product item
Both MOs have all ingredients picked
Pre-snapshot items.currentStockUnitCost for the product
seed_data: MO-A plannedQuantity=10 with ingredient cost yielding unitCost=8
MO-B plannedQuantity=5 with ingredient cost yielding unitCost=12

interaction_plan: Compute expected items.currentStockUnitCost INDEPENDENT of order: (10*8 + 5*12) / (10+5) = 140/15 = 9.333333
Fire two POST /complete in parallel via Promise.allSettled
Settle and assert both succeed

side_effects: Exactly 2 new lots rows for the product (one per MO) since produceManufacturedStockInTx creates a new lot when no lotId provided
items.currentStockUnitCost === expected weighted average AT SCALE 6 (computed from inputs, not observed order)
Both inventoryEvents of eventType='manufacturing_output' present with idempotencyKey non-null
COUNT of deadlock-retry events bounded — assert no 500 responses returned
negative_assertions: Neither response is 500 (no deadlock surface)
items.currentStockUnitCost is NOT equal to either MO-A-only or MO-B-only weighted average; it's the cumulative

flakiness_risks: Float precision: use parseFloat + toBeCloseTo(9.333333, 5) OR string equality after computing expected with the same formula.
On deadlock retry, kernel re-runs the tx — the final state should still be correct but if the retry is observed as 500 the test should still pass on a fresh re-run.
data_isolation_notes: Per-test ts; both MOs share the same productId but distinct ingredient lot ids.

review_focus: Are SAME-KEY replay specs (S19, S20) using explicit `headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': K }` overrides on BOTH calls, given that testFetch's default key changes when the body changes?
Are DISTINCT-key concurrency specs (S21) using DIFFERENT explicit Idempotency-Keys so the second call is not a replay?
Is S11's 500 assertion tight enough — exactly 500, with a TODO note for flag-flip when MissingCostBasisError handling lands?
Is S13's three-invariant assertion structured so the failure message explicitly names which invariant failed (lot decrement / ingredient restock / variance_gain event)?
Is S17's BR-10 absence assertion filtering audit_events by created_at > snapshotTime to avoid cross-test drift?
Are S05 and S23 (slow override vs fast first-attempt) clearly non-overlapping — S23 stops at the 409, S05 continues to the override and NEG-lot assertion?

Does S06 still need to be in the slow lane given it shares DAL surface with S05 and is now P1? (Critic: yes — it tests a distinct discriminator warningType='requirement_violation' and the requirementOverrideConfirmed metadata path.)
Are race scenarios (S21, S22) using response-shape-based winner identification, not array order?
